concepts.learning_objective: Write decimal fractions with denominators 10, 100, 1000 and their sums as decimals using place value.
Divide a whole number by 10, 100 or 1000 by moving the decimal point to the left.
Multiply decimals by multiplying the numbers without decimal points and placing the decimal point by counting decimal digits.
Predict whether a product of decimals is greater or less than the numbers multiplied.

topics.title: Decimal Division by 10, 100, 1000 and Equivalent Fractions

concepts.learning_objective: Divide a decimal by 10, 100 or 1000 by shifting the decimal point left.
Convert a fraction to a decimal by finding an equivalent fraction with denominator 10, 100, 1000 and so on.

topics.title: Long Division with Decimal Quotients, Dividends and Divisors

concepts.learning_objective: Use division by place value, regrouping Ones into Tenths and beyond, to find decimal quotients.
Divide by a decimal by multiplying the divisor and dividend by the same power of 10.

topics.title: Does This Ever End? Dividend, Divisor and Quotient

concepts.learning_objective: Recognise divisions whose decimal quotient never ends because remainders repeat.
Explore the repeating block 142857 of 1/7 and its cyclic multiples.
Compare the quotient with the dividend when dividing by numbers greater or less than 1.
Apply the rules of divisibility by 4, 100 and 400 to decide leap years.
Use decimal multiplication to compare calendar days with the Earth's actual revolution time.
